ECE 6390 / Antennas and arrays

Dipole patterns

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows why a straight dipole radiates strongly broadside and has an axial null.

The observation angle θ is measured from the wire axis. For an electrically short dipole, normalized far-field amplitude is sin θ and normalized intensity is sin²θ.

A thin half-wave dipole has the different amplitude factor cos[(π/2)cos θ]/sin θ, with its axial limit evaluated explicitly. Both models retain an axial null and a broadside maximum.

A cut normalized to a peak of 1 describes relative shape. Absolute directivity requires a solid-angle integral of intensity, and gain additionally depends on radiation efficiency and its power reference.

Example

For the short-dipole model at θ = 30°, field is one half the broadside value. Relative intensity is one quarter, approximately −6.02 dB.

Model and course sources

    Practice

    1. A short dipole's normalized field is 0.5 in a direction. What normalized power belongs there, and why?

    For the same wave impedance, intensity is proportional to squared field magnitude.

    Normalized power is |0.5|² = 0.25. A field-amplitude plot and a power-pattern plot consequently have different radial shapes.
